title: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness
body:
Read the chapter → [Leviticus 5](/bible/leviticus/5)

**[Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1)</sup> And if a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it; if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity.

- If a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it, if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity. Verse 4 defines the voice of swearing: a soul that swears, pronouncing with his lips to do evil or to do good. If you know and say nothing, your brother's blood is required because you did nothing about it.
- We are to rebuke one another. Hear no evil, see no evil, speak no evil is a wicked saying; the scriptures say you renounce evil. The watchman does not cover his eyes, because he needs to see, and does not cover his mouth, because he gives the warning; hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.
- If you do not apply this verse, you hate your brother in your heart; keeping quiet at his sin, or trimming your ways for him, is hate too. Stand still for the laws of the Most High and do not turn your ways for anybody, even carnal family that puts you out over your beard or your fringes.
- There is a way to correct: brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness. A soft answer turneth away wrath; you do not render evil for evil and blast a brother, you build him up with a humble mind, and that is how souls are won. The man gathering sticks got the reproof that fit that willful case; meekness fits the brother overtaken in a fault.

  Precepts:
  - **[Ezekiel 3:17](/bible/ezekiel/3#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/ezekiel/3#v17)</sup> Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.

    I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel; hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me.
  - **[Leviticus 19:17](/bible/leviticus/19#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/leviticus/19#v17)</sup> Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.

    Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart; not uttering what you witnessed is hating your brother.
  - **[Galatians 6:1](/bible/galatians/6#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/galatians/6#v1)</sup> Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.

    If a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; that is how you win souls.

- The witness law was written when Israel was in its own kingdom and everyone lived by the law; today it is applied among those in the body that understand the law, not to the world outside. The Most High judges them that are without, so the neighbor selling drugs on the corner is not your business; but when you see sin among Israel, do not hide it, bring it out, send it up to the leadership or correct it yourself. The land full of bloody crimes is what came upon Jerusalem when this law was not applied among the people.
- A lot of people do not know how to apply this verse; the precept for [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1) is [Deuteronomy 17:4](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v4). Whether the thing be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and only when it be true and the thing certain does judgment proceed: make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 17:4](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v4)</sup> And it be told thee, and thou hast heard of it, and enquired diligently, and, behold, it be true, and the thing certain, that such abomination is wrought in Israel:

    Enquire diligently, and behold, if it be true and the thing certain; the diligent enquiry that governs how the witness law is applied.
  - **[1 Corinthians 5:9-13](/bible/1-corinthians/5#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/1-corinthians/5#v9)</sup> I wrote unto you in an epistle not to company with fornicators:
    >
    > <sup>[10](/bible/1-corinthians/5#v10)</sup> Yet not altogether with the fornicators of this world, or with the covetous, or extortioners, or with idolaters; for then must ye needs go out of the world.
    >
    > <sup>[11](/bible/1-corinthians/5#v11)</sup> But now I have written unto you not to keep company, if any man that is called a brother be a fornicator, or covetous, or an idolater, or a railer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner; with such an one no not to eat.
    >
    > <sup>[12](/bible/1-corinthians/5#v12)</sup> For what have I to do to judge them also that are without? do not ye judge them that are within?
    >
    > <sup>[13](/bible/1-corinthians/5#v13)</sup> But them that are without God judgeth. Therefore put away from among yourselves that wicked person.

    What have I to do to judge them also that are without? them that are without God judgeth; the law is applied among the body, not the world.
  - **[Proverbs 28:17](/bible/proverbs/28#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/proverbs/28#v17)</sup> A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him.

    A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him; do not hide sin among Israel, bring it out.
  - **[Ezekiel 7:21-23](/bible/ezekiel/7#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/ezekiel/7#v21)</sup> And I will give it into the hands of the strangers for a prey, and to the wicked of the earth for a spoil; and they shall pollute it.
    >
    > <sup>[22](/bible/ezekiel/7#v22)</sup> My face will I turn also from them, and they shall pollute my secret place: for the robbers shall enter into it, and defile it.
    >
    > <sup>[23](/bible/ezekiel/7#v23)</sup> Make a chain: for the land is full of bloody crimes, and the city is full of violence.

    Make a chain, for the land is full of bloody crimes; that is what came upon Jerusalem when this law was not applied among the people.

**[Leviticus 5:2-3](/bible/leviticus/5#v2)**

> <sup>[2](/bible/leviticus/5#v2)</sup> Or if a soul touch any unclean thing, whether it be a carcase of an unclean beast, or a carcase of unclean cattle, or the carcase of unclean creeping things, and if it be hidden from him; he also shall be unclean, and guilty.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/leviticus/5#v3)</sup> Or if he touch the uncleanness of man, whatsoever uncleanness it be that a man shall be defiled withal, and it be hid from him; when he knoweth of it, then he shall be guilty.

- Touching any unclean thing, the carcase of an unclean beast or the uncleanness of man, leaves a soul unclean and guilty. This goes into eating, not mere contact; the classes have touched on this already, and it stands.
- It is the same as telling your son or daughter, get your hand out of the cookie jar: you say do not touch it, not do not eat it, because you know what the intention is. The Lord deals with us the same way; do not be touching that stuff means do not eat it, do not defile yourself.
- The touching itself pertained to the sacrifice: Israel was separated from their uncleanness that they die not when they defile the tabernacle, so a man that had touched the unclean thing could not come in to sacrifice. There is no more sacrifice, so the touching-defilement laws do not apply today; a brush of boar bristles is not sin.

  Precepts:
  - **[Leviticus 15:31](/bible/leviticus/15#v31)**
    > <sup>[31](/bible/leviticus/15#v31)</sup> Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness; that they die not in their uncleanness, when they defile my tabernacle that is among them.

    Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not, when they defile my tabernacle; the defilement laws guarded the sacrifice.

**[Leviticus 5:4-6](/bible/leviticus/5#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/leviticus/5#v4)</sup> Or if a soul swear, pronouncing with his lips to do evil, or to do good, whatsoever it be that a man shall pronounce with an oath, and it be hid from him; when he knoweth of it, then he shall be guilty in one of these.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/leviticus/5#v5)</sup> And it shall be, when he shall be guilty in one of these things, that he shall confess that he hath sinned in that thing:
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/leviticus/5#v6)</sup> And he shall bring his trespass offering unto the Lord for his sin which he hath sinned, a female from the flock, a lamb or a kid of the goats, for a sin offering; and the priest shall make an atonement for him concerning his sin.

- If a soul swear, pronouncing with his lips to do evil or to do good, and it be hid from him, when he knoweth of it he is guilty. Brothers say, I swear to God; watch your mouth.
- When a man is guilty in one of these things, he shall confess that he hath sinned in that thing, and bring his trespass offering, a female from the flock, a lamb or a kid of the goats, and the priest shall make an atonement for him concerning his sin.
- A man was held accountable for whatever came out of his mouth; pronouncing with his lips and not performing it was sin. When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it, for better is it that thou shouldest not vow than that thou shouldest vow and not pay; suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin. Christ set the same standard on the mouth: let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay.

  Precepts:
  - **[Ecclesiastes 5:4-6](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v4)</sup> When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v5)</sup> Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
    >
    > <sup>[6](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v6)</sup> Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?

    Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay; suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin.
  - **[Matthew 5:37](/bible/matthew/5#v37)**
    > <sup>[37](/bible/matthew/5#v37)</sup> But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.

    Let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.

**[Leviticus 5:7-13](/bible/leviticus/5#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/leviticus/5#v7)</sup> And if he be not able to bring a lamb, then he shall bring for his trespass, which he hath committed, two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, unto the Lord; one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/leviticus/5#v8)</sup> And he shall bring them unto the priest, who shall offer that which is for the sin offering first, and wring off his head from his neck, but shall not divide it asunder:
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/leviticus/5#v9)</sup> And he shall sprinkle of the blood of the sin offering upon the side of the altar; and the rest of the blood shall be wrung out at the bottom of the altar: it is a sin offering.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/leviticus/5#v10)</sup> And he shall offer the second for a burnt offering, according to the manner: and the priest shall make an atonement for him for his sin which he hath sinned, and it shall be forgiven him.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/leviticus/5#v11)</sup> But if he be not able to bring two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, then he that sinned shall bring for his offering the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering; he shall put no oil upon it, neither shall he put any frankincense thereon: for it is a sin offering.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/leviticus/5#v12)</sup> Then shall he bring it to the priest, and the priest shall take his handful of it, even a memorial thereof, and burn it on the altar, according to the offerings made by fire unto the Lord: it is a sin offering.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/leviticus/5#v13)</sup> And the priest shall make an atonement for him as touching his sin that he hath sinned in one of these, and it shall be forgiven him: and the remnant shall be the priest’s, as a meat offering.

- The offering scaled to what a man could bring: if he be not able to bring a lamb, two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering; and if he be not able to bring those, the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour, with no oil and no frankincense upon it, for it is a sin offering.
- The offerings were the collateral of those times, and families felt the after-effects of always sacrificing: the livestock and the agriculture went for your sins, and the household lacked because of it.
- Israel took the nourishment of the Lord for granted, and he grew tired of the empty offerings: put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh. He spake not unto our fathers concerning burnt offerings, but this thing commanded he: obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people. He never wanted the sacrifices above obedience; today he does not want an apology or money in the plate, he wants you to obey his voice and repent.

  Precepts:
  - **[Jeremiah 7:21-23](/bible/jeremiah/7#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/jeremiah/7#v21)</sup> Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, and eat flesh.
    >
    > <sup>[22](/bible/jeremiah/7#v22)</sup> For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices:
    >
    > <sup>[23](/bible/jeremiah/7#v23)</sup> But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you.

    Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices; I commanded not burnt offerings, but this thing: obey my voice, and I will be your God.

**[Leviticus 5:14-16](/bible/leviticus/5#v14)**

> <sup>[14](/bible/leviticus/5#v14)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/leviticus/5#v15)</sup> If a soul commit a trespass, and sin through ignorance, in the holy things of the Lord; then he shall bring for his trespass unto the Lord a ram without blemish out of the flocks, with thy estimation by shekels of silver, after the shekel of the sanctuary, for a trespass offering:
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/leviticus/5#v16)</sup> And he shall make amends for the harm that he hath done in the holy thing, and shall add the fifth part thereto, and give it unto the priest: and the priest shall make an atonement for him with the ram of the trespass offering, and it shall be forgiven him.

- If a soul commit a trespass and sin through ignorance in the holy things of the Lord, he brings a ram without blemish, with thy estimation by shekels of silver after the shekel of the sanctuary; he makes amends for the harm done in the holy thing and adds the fifth part thereto for the priest, and it shall be forgiven him.
- The scripture that pops up again is the same one: if thou sayest, behold, we knew it not, doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? Worldly family and coworkers that are not keeping the laws talk the same way, not understanding they condemn themselves because they are not repenting; that card cannot be pulled on the Messiah.

  Precepts:
  - **[Proverbs 24:12](/bible/proverbs/24#v12)**
    > <sup>[12](/bible/proverbs/24#v12)</sup> If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?

    Doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? He that keepeth thy soul knoweth whether the ignorance is real.

**[Leviticus 5:17-19](/bible/leviticus/5#v17)**

> <sup>[17](/bible/leviticus/5#v17)</sup> And if a soul sin, and commit any of these things which are forbidden to be done by the commandments of the Lord; though he wist it not, yet is he guilty, and shall bear his iniquity.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/leviticus/5#v18)</sup> And he shall bring a ram without blemish out of the flock, with thy estimation, for a trespass offering, unto the priest: and the priest shall make an atonement for him concerning his ignorance wherein he erred and wist it not, and it shall be forgiven him.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/leviticus/5#v19)</sup> It is a trespass offering: he hath certainly trespassed against the Lord.

- If a soul sin against any of the commandments, though he wist it not, yet is he guilty, and shall bear his iniquity. Though he is ignorant of it, the iniquity is still there; saying I did not know does not remove sin, and everyone still appears before the judgment seat of Christ when it is all said and done. The priest made an atonement concerning his ignorance wherein he erred and wist it not, for he hath certainly trespassed against the Lord.
- The remedy is to know the law: let thy mind be upon the ordinances of the Lord, and meditate continually in his commandments. The ordinances are found in the first five books; as these four chapters a day are conducted, meditate and study them continually.
- As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby. The milk is the dos and the don'ts. Many want to run to Revelation and the parables, but the solutions for what is wrong in your spirit, for lust, covetousness, hatred, malice, and envy, sit in the ordinances and the commandments; look up the scriptures on patience, temperance, and how to treat your family correctly.
- Stay humble with it: Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty; neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me; David behaved and quieted himself as a child that is weaned of his mother. Except ye be converted and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven; so behave yourselves humbly, and the Most High will establish thine heart and increase thy wisdom.

  Precepts:
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 6:37](/bible/sirach/6#v37)**
    > <sup>[37](/bible/sirach/6#v37)</sup> Let thy mind be upon the ordinances of the Lord and meditate continually in his commandments: he shall establish thine heart, and give thee wisdom at thine owns desire.

    Meditate continually in his commandments, and he shall establish thine heart and give thee wisdom.
  - **[1 Peter 2:2](/bible/1-peter/2#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/1-peter/2#v2)</sup> As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby:

    As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby; the milk is the first five books.
  - **[Psalms 131:1-2](/bible/psalms/131#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/psalms/131#v1)</sup> Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty: neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/psalms/131#v2)</sup> Surely I have behaved and quieted myself, as a child that is weaned of his mother: my soul is even as a weaned child.

    My heart is not haughty; I have behaved and quieted myself as a child that is weaned of his mother.
  - **[Matthew 18:1-3](/bible/matthew/18#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/matthew/18#v1)</sup> At the same time came the disciples unto Jesus, saying, Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/matthew/18#v2)</sup> And Jesus called a little child unto him, and set him in the midst of them,
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/matthew/18#v3)</sup> And said, Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.

    Except ye be converted and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.
